//: Nothing here emits: every project sets `noEmit` and no `outDir` exists in the tree. The three runtimes read the TypeScript directly — Vite/wrangler bundle the Worker, Bun runs the CLI and the suites from source, and the deploy ships a source archive. So `moduleResolution: bundler` is not a preference, it is the only resolver that describes what actually happens, and an import specifier names a module rather than a build output. `allowImportingTsExtensions` is deliberately ABSENT: it belongs only to the two projects holding raw-Node files (tools/oxlint/anti-slop, scripts), and its absence here is what makes tsc reject a `.ts` specifier everywhere else.
//plugins: The Effect language service reads the `plugins` entry; plain `tsc` ignores it. `gate:effect-diagnostics` runs the pinned @effect/tsgo with it over every project that imports `effect`, and fails if its planted floating effect goes unreported.
